td_sequential.reference: Tom DeMark TD Setup / TD Sequential as documented in Jason Perl, 'DeMark Indicators' (2008); countdown qualifier, cancellation and recycle rule I as summarised at https://oxfordstrat.com/indicators/td-sequential-3/

strategy_issues.issue: The 'sequential' is only the consecutive close > close[4] streak, wrapping from 13 back to 1. It trades buySetup == 13 / sellSetup == 13 as if it were a TD Countdown 13, but there is no setup completion at 9 and no close <= low[2] countdown. Reproduced by buy_count / sell_count ((count-1) % 13 + 1).
Same as c25f0dd3006d for the buy side.

td_sequential.notes: buy_count / sell_count are the plain streaks the FMZ copies call TD (ids 28951d1604e0, 41fe9f1aa056, fb3a692ce0dd, ad23467a7a82); they match bar for bar. TDUp = TD - valuewhen(TD < TD[1], TD, 1) in the copies equals TD once two resets have happened (TD only drops by resetting to 0). The proper TD Setup (buy_setup) needs the price flip close[1] > close[5] and is complete at 9, with perfection and TDST. Also implemented: TD Countdown (close <= low[2], 13th bar qualified by low <= close of countdown bar 8, deferred otherwise), cancellation by an opposite setup or a true low above TDST, and recycle rule I (TR1 <= TR2 < 1.618*TR1). Not modelled: recycle rules II/III and TD Combo. Tested against a separate bar-by-bar port of these rules.

strategy_issues.issue: linregs() computes b = sum((x - xbar)*(y - ybar), len) / sum((x - xbar)^2, len) with xbar and ybar as series, so each bar's deviation uses that bar's own rolling mean instead of the current window's mean. The result is not the OLS slope; the test checks that it differs. a = ybar - b*xbar inherits the error.

avellaneda_stoikov_bands.reference: model='tamim': 'Khaled Tamim's Avellaneda-Stoikov Strategy' (FMZ copy). model='as2008': Avellaneda & Stoikov (2008), 'High-frequency trading in a limit order book', Quantitative Finance 8(3).

strategy_issues.issue: Not the Avellaneda-Stoikov model: the quotes are mid -+ k*gamma*sigma^2*T, with no inventory term, no time decay and no (2/gamma)ln(1+gamma/k) spread. 'k' is used as a plain multiplier, and sigma=8 is in price units. Ported as written (default model) and labelled.

avellaneda_stoikov_bands.notes: The real model is offered as model='as2008' with constant T and a user inventory q: reservation price r = close - q*gamma*sigma^2*T; quotes r -+ (gamma*sigma^2*T + (2/gamma)ln(1+gamma/k))/2.

adaptive_trailing_stop.reference: 'Wilder's Volatility Trailing Stop Strategy with various MA's' by SparkyFlary (FMZ 适应性趋势跟踪止损策略); concept from Wilder's Volatility System (New Concepts, 1978)

strategy_issues.issue: 'float TS = 0' is not var, so the ': TS' branch of 'TS := close < TS[1] ? upperTrail[1] : close > TS[1] ? lowerTrail[1] : TS' yields 0. The stop drops to 0 on any bar whose close equals the previous stop, and it alternates 0 / na during warm-up. Fixed: the stop holds its previous value.

adaptive_trailing_stop.notes: upper = lowest(close or low, n) + mult*ATR and lower = highest(close or high, n) - mult*ATR, with ATR = rma/ema/sma/hma of tr. Matches the script on every bar where the script's stop is not 0/na. Wilder's own system uses the extreme close since entry, not a rolling window.

dual_thrust.reference: Dual Thrust (Michael Chalek); QuantConnect tutorial https://www.quantconnect.com/tutorials/strategy-library/dual-thrust-trading-algorithm; capissimo 'Dual Thrust Trading Algorithm (ps4)' for the asymmetric Algo #2
dual_thrust.notes: Range = max(HH - LC, HC - LL) over the previous N bars (current bar excluded); triggers are open + k1*range and open - k2*range. sell_length > 0 gives Algo #2's separate sell lookback. faf73a411400 and 8eae2812800a match. capissimo's trend rule that scales k1/k2 is not part of Dual Thrust and is left out. Chalek's system uses daily ranges with intraday entries: compute on daily bars and map down with a higher-timeframe helper.

standard_error_bands.reference: Jon Andersen, 'Standard Error Bands', TASC Sept 1996 (21-period linear regression, 2 standard errors, 3-period SMA smoothing)

strategy_issues.issue: The 'narrow' band is the correct standard error, but computed as sum(y^2) - a*sum(y) - b*sum(x*y) with x = bar_index. That cancels large numbers and loses precision on long histories or high prices (it can even go negative and give NaN). The 'wide' band (sum((linreg - close)^2)/(n-2), residuals against each bar's own endpoint) is not a standard error at all.

standard_error_bands.notes: SEE is computed from the residuals around each window's regression line (numerically stable). Matches the copy's narrow band to 1e-5 relative.

adaptive_trend_flow.notes: Defaults are QuantAlgo's (10, 14, 2.0); the FMZ copy (bfde7300f106) uses 2 / 2 / 2.0 with SMA and MACD filters around it. Outputs: basis, upper, lower, trend and level.
